name: Hazard Volume
description: Regions of the world that hurt on contact — spikes, lava, a bottomless pit's kill plane. It reports the contact and nothing else: it does not damage anyone, move anyone, or end anything. What happens next is the business of whatever listens, which is why the same spike can kill in one build and cost a heart in another without this component changing. retriggerSeconds exists because a volume tested every frame fires sixty times a second otherwise, and a hazard that hits sixty times is not a hazard, it is a crash. world.hazardEntered carries the `impact` intent, so a build with particles, audio or a screen shake gets all three reacting to it without wiring any of them. For multi-volume boss arenas, hazardId and a monotonically increasing contactCount give each contact a stable contactId. Damage remains intent data; an opt-in Damage Resolver mode may resolve nonlethal contact damage, while this volume still never writes health.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: regions
inputs.description: Rectangles in world units, each {x, y, width, height}. Required with no default: a hazard with no regions is an unconfigured build, not a sensible empty one.

inputs.name: damage
inputs.description: Carried on the event for a listener that wants it. This component does not apply it — it has no opinion about health.

inputs.name: retriggerSeconds
inputs.description: How long after a contact before the same body can trigger again. Doubles as the invulnerability window a player expects after being hit.

inputs.name: instantlyLethal
inputs.description: Carried on the event. True is a pit or spikes; false is a hazard that chips away at health and needs something tracking it.

inputs.name: hazardId
inputs.description: Stable per-instance id included in world.hazardEntered. Arena Hazards supplies the authored hazard id for each volume it controls.

inputs.name: initialContactCount
inputs.description: Restored contact ordinal used to continue stable contact ids without emitting a historical contact.

outputs.name: lastContact
outputs.description: Latest hazardId, bodyId, contactId, damage, instantlyLethal, and impact intent. Contact is a fact, not a completed damage resolution.
